questions.a: Two or more substances mixed in any proportion, each keeping its own properties - like air or salt water.

questions.q: Name the two kinds of mixtures.
questions.a: Homogeneous (uniform, e.g. sugar solution) and heterogeneous (non-uniform, e.g. sand and salt).

questions.q: Why is a mixture called an impure substance?
questions.a: It has no fixed composition and contains more than one substance.
Matter of only one kind of particle - an element or a compound - with fixed properties.

questions.q: How do elements and compounds differ?
questions.a: Elements have one kind of atom (iron, oxygen); compounds join different atoms in fixed ratios (water).

questions.q: Is distilled water a pure substance? Why?
questions.a: Yes - it contains only water molecules with nothing dissolved.

questions.q: What is an element? Give two examples.
questions.a: A substance of one kind of atom that cannot be broken chemically - iron and oxygen (also gold, hydrogen).

questions.q: Name the three classes of elements.
questions.a: Metals, non-metals and metalloids (properties between both).

questions.q: What is a compound? Give two examples.
questions.a: Two or more elements chemically joined in fixed ratio - water (H2O) and carbon dioxide (CO2).

questions.q: Why do we use alloys when pure metals exist?
questions.a: Alloys mix metals for strength, shine or rust-resistance - brass, steel, bronze.

questions.q: Give one use each of a compound and a mixture in daily life.
questions.a: Compound: salt (NaCl) in food. Mixture: air we breathe, or steel in construction.

questions.q: Which is easier to separate - a mixture or a compound? Why?
questions.a: A mixture - simple physical methods work (filtering, magnet); compounds need chemical reactions.
Naturally occurring substances in rocks and ores from which metals and other materials are obtained.

questions.q: Name two minerals important in food.
questions.a: Iron and calcium (also iodine) - needed by our body in small amounts.

questions.q: How do we obtain metals from minerals?
questions.a: By mining the ore and extracting the metal through heating or electrolysis.
